pp:me:2014:q1.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 1
pp:me:2014:q1.question:
Given that the determinant of the matrix
$$\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 & 0\\ 2 & 6 & 4\\ -1 & 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$$
is -12, the determinant of the matrix
$$\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 6 & 0\\ 4 & 12 & 8\\ -2 & 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$$

detailed_solution.markdown:
Let D=-12 for the given matrix

$$|A|=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}2 & 6 & 0 \\4 & 12 & 8 \\-2 & 0 & 4\end{array}\right|=(2)^{3}\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & 3 & 0 \\2 & 6 & 4 \\-1 & 0 & 2\end{array}\right|$$

(Taking 2 common from each row)

$$\begin{aligned}\therefore \text{Det}(A) &=(2)^{3} \times D \\=& 8 x-12=-96\end{aligned}$$

$\lim_{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{x-\sin x}{1-\cos x}$

Applying L ' Hospital's rule

$\lim_{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\frac{d}{dx}(x-sinx)}{\frac{d}{dx}(1-cosx)}=\lim_{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{(1-\cos x)}{\sin x}$

(It is still of $\frac{0}{0}$ form)

Again applying L' Hospital's rule

$\lim_{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\frac{d}{d x}(1-\cos x)}{\frac{d}{d x}(\sin x)}=\lim_{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}=\frac{0}{1}=0$

pp:me:2014:q3.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 3
pp:me:2014:q3.question: The argument of the complex number $\frac{1+i}{1-i}$,where $i=\sqrt{-1}$, is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} Let z&=\frac{1+i}{1-i} \\ or z&=\frac{(1+i)(1+i)}{(1-i)(1+i)}=\frac{1+i^{2}+2 i}{1-i^{2}}=\frac{2 i}{2}=i \\ z&=x+i y=i \\ SO, x&=0 \\ y &=1 \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} Arg(z) &=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right) \\ &=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{0}\right)=\tan ^{-1} \infty=\frac{\pi}{2} \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2014:q4.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 4
pp:me:2014:q4.question: The matrix form of the linear system $\frac{dx}{dt}=3x-5y$ and $\frac{dy}{dt}=4x+8y$ is

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} \frac{d x}{d t} &=3 x-5 y \\ \frac{d y}{d t} &=4 x+8 y \\ \frac{d}{d t}\left\{\begin{array}{l}x \\y\end{array}\right\}&=\left[\begin{array}{cc}3 & -5 \\4 & 8\end{array}\right]\left\{\begin{array}{l}x \\y\end{array}\right\}=\left[\begin{array}{cc} 3 x & -5 y \\4 x & +8 y\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}$$

detailed_solution.markdown:
For linear dependency, det $$\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 5 & 6 & 4\end{array}\right|$$ must be zero.

$=6-3-3=0$

pp:me:2014:q7.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 7
pp:me:2014:q7.question: A mentalic rod of 500 mm length and 50mm diameter, when subjected to a tensile force of 100KN at the ends, experiences an increase in its length by 0.5 mm and a reduction in its diameter by 0.015 m. the poission's ratio of the rod material is_________

detailed_solution.concept: Strength of Materials - Stress-strain Relationship and Elastic Constants
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{array}{l} v=-\frac{\text { Lateral strain }}{\text { Longitudinal strain }}=-\frac{\left(\frac{\Delta D}{D}\right)}{\left(\frac{\Delta L}{L}\right)} \\ v=\left(\frac{L}{D}\right)\left(-\frac{\Delta D}{\Delta L}\right) \\ \text{given,}L=500\mathrm{mm},D=50\mathrm{mm}\\ \Delta D=-0.015, \Delta L=+0.5 \mathrm{mm} \\ \qquad v=\frac{500}{50} \times \frac{0.015}{0.500}=0.3 \end{array}$$

pp:me:2014:q8.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 8
pp:me:2014:q8.question: Critical damping is the
options: largest amount of damping for which no oscillation occurs in free vibration
smallest amount of damping for which no oscillation occurs in free vibration
largest amount of damping for which the motion is simple harmonic in free vibration
smallest amount of damping for which the motion is simple harmonic in free vibration

detailed_solution.markdown: The system with critical damping returns to equilibrium in fastest time without any oscillation. pp:me:2014:q26.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 26
pp:me:2014:q26.question: The integral $\oint_c (ydx-xdy)$  is evalulated along the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=\frac{1}{4}$ traversed in counter clockwise direction. The integral is equal to

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} \int_{C}(\phi d x+\psi d y) &=\iint_{E}\left(\frac{\partial \psi}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial \phi}{\partial y}\right) d x d y \\ \phi &=y \\ \psi &=-x \\ \frac{\partial \psi}{\partial x} &=-1 \\ \frac{\partial \phi}{\partial y} &=1 \\ I &=\iint_{E}\left(\frac{\partial \psi}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial \phi}{\partial y}\right) d x d y \\ &=\int_{0}^{1 / 2} \int_{0}^{2 \pi}(-2) r d \theta d r \\ &=-2\left(\int_{0}^{1 / 2} r d r\right)\left(\int_{0}^{2 \pi} r d \theta\right) \\ &=-2\left(\frac{r^{2}}{2}\right)_{0}^{1 / 2} 2 \pi=-\frac{\pi}{2} \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2014:q27.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 27
pp:me:2014:q27.question: If $y=f(x)$  is the solution of $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}=0$$ with the boundary conditions y=5 at x=0, and  $\frac{dy}{dx}=2$ at x=10, f(15)=_____

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} \frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}} &=0 \\ \frac{d y}{d x} &=C_{1} \\ \Rightarrow \qquad C_{1} &=2 \\ y &=C_{1} x+C_{2} \\ at \qquad x &=0 ; \quad y=5=C_{2} \\ \therefore \qquad y &=2 x+5 \\ at \qquad y(15) &=2 \times 15+5=35 \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2014:q29.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 29
pp:me:2014:q29.question: Using the trapezoidal rule, and dividing the interval of integration into three equal subintervals, the definite integral $\int_{-1}^{+1}\left | x \right |dx$  is ___________

detailed_solution.markdown: $I=\int_{-1}^{1}|x| \mathrm{d} x$ $n=3, h=\frac{1-(-1)}{3}=\frac{2}{3}$ By Trapezoidal rule $\int_{-1}^{1}|x| d x=\frac{h}{2}\left[\left(y_{0}+y_{3}\right)+2\left(y_{1}+y_{2}\right)\right]$ $=\frac{2}{3 \times 2}\left[(1+1)+2\left(\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3}\right)\right]$ $=\frac{1}{3}\left[2+\frac{4}{3}\right]=1.11$

pp:me:2014:q30.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 30
pp:me:2014:q30.question: The state of stress at a point is given by  $\sigma_{x}$= -6Mpa, $\sigma_{y}$=4 MPa  and $\tau_{xy}$=-8 MPa . The maximum tensile stress (in MPa) at the point is _________

detailed_solution.concept: Strength of Materials - Stress-strain Relationship and Elastic Constants
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} \sigma_{1} &=\frac{\sigma_{x}+\sigma_{y}}{2}+\sqrt{\left(\frac{\sigma_{x}-\sigma_{y}}{2}\right)^{2}+\tau_{x y}^{2}} \\ &=\frac{+6-4}{2}+\sqrt{\left(\frac{+6-4}{2}\right)^{2}+(-8)^{2}} \\ &=-1+\sqrt{25+64} \\ &=-1+\sqrt{89}=8.4339 \mathrm{MPa} \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2014:q31.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 31
pp:me:2014:q31.question: A block R of mass 100kg is placed on a block S of mass 150kg as shown in the figure. Block R is tied to the wall by a massless and intextensible string PQ. pp:me:2014:q33.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 33
pp:me:2014:q33.question: Consider a cantilever beam, having negligible mass and uniform flexural rigidity, with length  0.01 m. The frequency of vibration of the beam, with a 0.5 kg mass attached at the free tip, is  100 Hz. The flexural rigidity (in N.$m^{2}$ ) of the beam is _______

detailed_solution.concept: Strength of Materials - Bending of Beams
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} P &=m g=0.5 \times 9.81=4.905 N \\ L &=0.01 \mathrm{m} \\ f_{n} &=100 \mathrm{Hz} \\ \omega_{n} &=2 \pi f_{n}=628 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \\ \omega_{n} &=\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}\\ \text { or } \quad k&=m \omega_{n}^{2}=0.5 \times(628)^{2}\\ &=197192 \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{m}\\ \delta &=\frac{P L^{3}}{3 E I} \\ \Rightarrow \frac{P}{\delta} &=\frac{3 E I}{L^{3}} \\ \text{or}\quad EI&=\frac{P}{\delta }\times\frac{L^{3}}{3}\\ &=197192 \times \frac{(0.01)^{3}}{3} \\ &=0.06573 \mathrm{Nm}^{2} \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2014:q34.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 34
pp:me:2014:q34.question: An ideal water jet with volume flow rate of 0.05 $m^{3}/s$  strikes a flat plate placed normal to its path and exerts a force of 1000 N. Considering the density of water as 1000 $kg/m^{3}$, the diameter (in mm) of the water jet is  _______

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} Q &=0.05 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{s} \\ F &=1000 \mathrm{N} \\ \rho &=1000 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \end{aligned}$$ $F=\rho a V^{2}$ where a= cross-section area fo the jet $$\begin{aligned} Q&=a V \\ \therefore \quad F&=\rho Q V \\ 1000 &=1000 \times 0.05 \times V \\ \text{or}\quad V &=20 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ Q &=a V \\ Q &=\frac{\pi}{4} d^{2} V \\ \text{or}\quad 0.05&=\frac{3.14}{4} \times d^{2} \times 20 \\ \text{or}\quad d^{2}&=0.00318 \\ d&=0.05643 \mathrm{m} \\&=56.43mm \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2014:q35.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 35
pp:me:2014:q35.question: A block weighing 200 N is in contact with a level plane whose coefficients of static and kinetic friction are 0.4 and 0.2, respectively. The block is acted upon by a horizontal force (in newton) P=10t, where t denotes the time in seconds. The velocity (in m/s) of the block attained after  10 seconds is _______

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} N &=m g=200 \mathrm{N} \\(f_{s})_{max} &=\mu_{s} N \\ &=0.4 \times 200=80 \end{aligned}$$

upto $8 \sec [P=10 t] \rightarrow$ no motion

$\Rightarrow$ from 8 sec to 10 sec

$$\begin{aligned} f_{k} &=\mu_{k} N \\ &=0.2 \times 200=40 \mathrm{N} \end{aligned}$$

Average applied force

$=\frac{P_{\max }+P_{\min }}{2}$

$=\frac{100+80}{2}=90 \mathrm{N}$

Average resultant force = Avg. applied force kinetic friction

$=90-40=50 N$

Average acceration

$$\begin{aligned} &=\frac{50 \times 9.8}{200} \\ \Rightarrow \quad V &=u+a t\\ u&=0\\ a&=\frac{50 \times 9.8}{200} \\ t&=2 \text{second}\\ \therefore V&=\frac{50 \times 9.8}{200} \times 2=4.9 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$

When the crank angle (with respect to slider axis) is $30^{\circ}$ , the unbalanced force (in newton) normal to the slider axis is _______

pp:me:2014:q37.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 37
pp:me:2014:q37.question: An offset slider-crank mechanism is shown in the figure at an instant. Conventionally, the Quick Return Ratio (QRR) is considered to be greater than one. The value of QRR is _______

detailed_solution.concept: Theory of Machine - Dynamic Analysis of Slider-crank
detailed_solution.markdown:
Length of connecting rod: $l_{r}=40 \mathrm{mm}$

Crank radius: $r=20 \mathrm{mm}$

Eccentricity: $e=10 \mathrm{mm}$

$$\begin{aligned} &\phi=\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{e}{l+r}\right)-\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{e}{l-r}\right) \\ &=\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)-\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=20.4^{\circ} \\ &\mathrm{QRR}=\frac{\text { Time of advance stroke }}{\text { Time of return stroke }} \\ &=\left(\frac{\theta_{C}}{2 \pi N}\right)\left(\frac{2 \pi N}{\theta_{R}}\right) \\ &\mathrm{QRR} =\frac{\theta_{C}}{\theta_{R}}=\frac{180^{\circ}+\phi}{180^{\circ}-\phi} \\ &=\frac{180^{\circ}+20.4^{\circ}}{180^{\circ}-20.4^{\circ}}=1.25 \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2014:q38.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 38
pp:me:2014:q38.question: A rigid uniform rod AB of length L and mass m is hinged at C such that AC = L/3, CB = 2L/3. Ends A and B are supported by springs of spring constant k. The natural frequency of the system is given by

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} \theta &=\frac{y_{A}}{\left(\frac{L}{3}\right)}=\frac{y_{B}}{\left(\frac{2 L}{3}\right)} \\ I_{0} &=I_{C}+m\left(\frac{2 L}{3}-\frac{L}{2}\right)^{2} \\ I_{C} &=\frac{m L^{2}}{12} \\ \therefore \quad I_{0} &=\frac{m L^{2}}{12}+\frac{m L^{2}}{36}=\frac{m L^{2}}{9} \end{aligned}$$ Taking, $\Sigma M_{0}=0$ $$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow\left(k y_{A} \times \frac{L}{3}\right)+\left(k y_{B} \times \frac{2 L}{3}\right)+I_{0} \ddot{\theta}=0 \\ \Rightarrow k \theta\left(\frac{L}{3}\right)^{2}+k \theta\left(\frac{2 L}{3}\right)^{2}+\frac{m L^{2}}{9} \ddot{\theta}=0 \\ \Rightarrow\left(\frac{m L^{2}}{9}\right) \ddot{\theta}+\left(\frac{5 k L^{2}}{9}\right) \theta=0 \\ \Rightarrow \ddot{\theta}+\left(\frac{5 k}{m}\right) \theta=0 \\ \omega_{n}^{2}=\frac{5 k}{m} \\ \quad \omega_{n}=\sqrt{\frac{5 k}{m}} \\ \end{array}$$

pp:me:2014:q39.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 39

pp:me:2014:q41.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 41
pp:me:2014:q41.question: 1.5 kg of water is in saturated liquid state at 2 bar ($v_{f}= 0.001061 m^3/kg$, $u_{f}$=504.0 kJ/kg,  $h_{f}$=505 kJ/kg). Heat is added in a constant pressure process till the temperature of water reaches 400$^{\circ}$C  (v=1.5493 $m^3$/kg, u = 2967.0 kJ/kg, h = 3277.0 kJ/kg). The heat added (in kJ) in the process is  _______

detailed_solution.markdown:
From the first law of thermodynamics

$$\begin{aligned} \delta q &=d u+p d v \\ \delta q &=\left(u_{2}-u_{1}\right)+p\left(v_{2}-v_{1}\right) \\ \delta q &=(2967-504)+2 \times 10^{2} \\ &(1.5493-0.001061) \\ \delta q &=2463+309.6478 \\ &=2772.6478 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned}$$

For 1.5kg of water

$$\begin{aligned} Q &=2772.6478 \times 1.5 \\ &=4158.97 \mathrm{kj} \end{aligned}$$

Alternatively:

$$\begin{aligned} Q &=m\left(h_{2}-h_{1}\right) \\ &=1.5(3277-505) \\ &=4158 \mathrm{kJ} \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2014:q42.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 42
pp:me:2014:q42.question: Consider one dimensional steady state heat conduction across a wall (as shown in figure below) of thickness 30 mm and thermal conductivity 15 W/m.K. At x = 0, a constant heat flux, $q''= 1\times 10^5 W/m^2$ is applied. On the other side of the wall, heat is removed from the wall by convection with a fluid at 25$^{\circ}$C and heat transfer coefficient of 250 $W/m^2$ K. The temperature (in $^{\circ}$C), at x = 0 is _______

detailed_solution.markdown: Given data: $$\begin{aligned} \delta&=30 \mathrm{mm}=0.03 \mathrm{m} ; \quad k=15 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{mK} \\ q^{\prime \prime}&=1 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2} ; \quad T_{\infty}=25^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ h&=250 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}$$ Heat transfer due to convection from outside surface per unit area: $$\begin{aligned} q^{\prime \prime} &=\frac{Q}{A}=h\left(T_{2}-T_{\infty}\right) \\ 1 \times 10^{5} &=250\left(T_{2}-25\right) \\ \text{or}\qquad T_{2} &=425^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \end{aligned}$$ Heat transfer through wall per unit area, $$\begin{aligned} q^{\prime \prime} &=\frac{k\left(T_{1}-T_{2}\right)}{\delta} \\ 1 \times 10^{5} &=\frac{15\left(T_{1}-425\right)}{0.03}\\ \text{or }\qquad T_{1}&=625^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2014:q43.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 43
pp:me:2014:q43.question: Water flows through a pipe having an inner radius of 10 mm at the rate of 36 kg/hr at 25$^{\circ}$C.  The viscosity of water at 25$^{\circ}$C is 0.001 kg/m.s.  The Reynolds number of the flow is _______

primary.subtopicLabel: Viscous, Turbulent Flow and Boundary Layer Theory

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics - Viscous, Turbulent Flow and Boundary Layer Theory
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Radius: }\quad r&=10 \mathrm{mm} \\ \therefore \text{Diameter: }d&=2 r=2 \times 10=20 \mathrm{mm}=0.02 \mathrm{m} \\ m &=36 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{hr}=\frac{36}{3600}=0.01 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \\ \mu &=0.001 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{ms} \end{aligned}$$

Reynolds number: $\text{Re}=\frac{\rho V d}{\mu}$

From continuity equation, $m=\rho A V$

$$\begin{aligned} \text{or }\quad V&=\frac{m}{\rho A}=\frac{m}{\frac{\rho \pi d^{2}}{4}}=\frac{4 m}{\rho \pi d^{2}} \\ \therefore \quad \mathrm{Re}&=\frac{\rho d}{\mu} \times \frac{4 \mathrm{m}}{\rho \pi d^{2}}=\frac{4 \mathrm{m}}{\pi \mu \mathrm{d}}\\ &=\frac{4 \times 0.01}{3.14 \times 0.001 \times 0.02}=636.94 \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2014:q44.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 44
pp:me:2014:q44.question: For a fully developed flow of water in a pipe having diameter 10 cm, velocity 0.1 m/s and kinematic viscosity $10^{-5}m^{2}/s$ , the value of Darcy friction factor is _______

primary.subtopicLabel: Viscous, Turbulent Flow and Boundary Layer Theory

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics - Viscous, Turbulent Flow and Boundary Layer Theory
detailed_solution.markdown:
Given data:

$$\begin{aligned} d&=10 \mathrm{cm} \\ V&=0.1 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ \mathrm{v}&=10^{-5} \mathrm{m}^{2} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$

Reynold's number,

$\mathrm{Re}=\frac{V d}{v}=\frac{0.1 \times 0.1}{10^{-5}}=1000$

Friction factor

$f=\frac{64}{\mathrm{Re}}=\frac{64}{1000}=0.064$

pp:me:2014:q45.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 45
pp:me:2014:q45.question: In a simple concentric shaft-bearing arrangement, the lubricant flows in the 2 mm gap between the shaft and the bearing. The flow may be assumed to be a plane Couette flow with zero pressure gradient. The diameter of the shaft is 100 mm and its tangential speed is 10 m/s. The dynamic viscosity of the lubricant is 0.1 kg/m.s. The frictional resisting force (in newton) per 100 mm length of the bearing is  _______

primary.subtopicLabel: Viscous, Turbulent Flow and Boundary Layer Theory

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics - Viscous, Turbulent Flow and Boundary Layer Theory
detailed_solution.markdown:
Given data:

$$\begin{aligned} d &=100 \mathrm{mm}=0.1 \mathrm{m} \\ L &=100 \mathrm{mm}=0.1 \mathrm{m} \\ u &=10 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ \mu &=0.1 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{ms} \\ d y &=2 \mathrm{mm}=2 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{m} \\ \tau &=\mu \frac{\mathrm{d} \mathrm{u}}{\mathrm{d} \mathrm{y}} \\ &=0.1 \times \frac{10}{2 \times 10^{-3}}=500 \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ \text{Frictional area }&= \pi dL=3.14 \times0.1 \times 0.1\\ &=0.0314 \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}$$

Frictional resistance force,

$$\begin{aligned} &=\tau \times \pi \mathrm{d} L \\ &=500 \times 0.0314=15.7 \mathrm{N} \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2014:q46.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 46
pp:me:2014:q46.question: The non-dimensional fluid temperature profile near the surface of a convectively cooled flat plate is given by $\frac{T_W-T}{T_W-T_\infty }=a+b\frac{y}{L}+c\left ( \frac{y}{L} \right )^2$, where y is measured perpendicular to the plate, $L$  is the plate length, and a, b and c are arbitrary constants. $T_{W}$  and $T_{\infty}$  are wall and ambient temperatures, respectively. If the thermal conductivity of the fluid is $k$   and the wall heat flux is $q''$, the Nusselt number $N_u=\frac{q''}{T_W-T_\infty }\frac{L}{k}$  is  equal to

primary.subtopicLabel: Heat Transfer in Flow Over Plates and Pipes

detailed_solution.concept: Heat Transfer - Heat Transfer in Flow Over Plates and Pipes
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} q^{\prime \prime} &=-\left.k \frac{\partial T}{\partial y}\right|_{y=0} \\ &=h\left(T_{w}-T_{\infty}\right) \\ T_{w}-T &=\left(T_{w}-T_{\infty}\right)\left[a+\frac{b y}{L}+c\left(\frac{y}{L}\right)^{2}\right] \\ \frac{\partial T}{\partial y} & =\left(T_{w}-T_{\infty}\right)\left[\frac{b}{L}+\frac{2 c}{L^{2}} y\right] \\ -\left.\frac{\partial T}{\partial y}\right|_{y=0} &=\left(T_{w}-T_{\infty}\right) \frac{b}{L} \\ \text{or} \quad q^{\prime \prime}&=k\left(T_{w}-T_{\infty}\right) \frac{b}{L} \\ \therefore \quad N u &=\frac{q^{\prime \prime}}{T_{w}-T_{\infty}} \frac{L}{k}=b \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2014:q47.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 47
pp:me:2014:q47.question: In an air-standard Otto cycle, air is supplied at 0.1 MPa and 308 K. The ratio of the specific heats ($\gamma$ ) and the specific gas constant (R) of air are 1.4 and 288.8 J/kg.K, respectively. If the compression ratio is 8 and the maximum temperature in the cycle is 2660 K, the heat (in kJ/kg) supplied to the engine is _______

detailed_solution.markdown: Given: $$\begin{aligned} p_{1}&=0.1 \mathrm{MPa} ; \quad T_{1}=308 \mathrm{K} ; \quad \gamma=1.4 \\ R&=288.8 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kgK} ; \quad r=8 \\ T_{s}&=2660 \mathrm{K} \\ &\begin{aligned} Q_{s}&=m c_{v}\left(T_{3}-T_{2}\right) \\ c_{v}&=\frac{R}{\gamma-1}=\frac{288.8}{0.4}=722 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}&=\left(\frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}\right)^{\gamma-1}=(8)^{0.4}\\ T_{2} &=308 \times 8^{0.4}=707.6 \mathrm{K} \\ Q_{s} &=m c_{v} \Delta T \\ &=1 \times 722(2660-707.6) \\ &=1409.6 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned} \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2014:q48.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 48
pp:me:2014:q48.question: A reversible heat engine receives 2 kJ of heat from a reservoir at 1000 K and a certain amount of heat from a reservoir at 800 K. It rejects 1 kJ of heat to a reservoir at 400 K. The network output (in kJ) of the cycle is

primary.subtopicLabel: Second Law, Carnot Cycle and Entropy

detailed_solution.concept: Thermodynamics - Second Law, Carnot Cycle and Entropy
detailed_solution.markdown: For reversible heat engine, $$\begin{aligned} (\Delta S)_{\text{ Reversible cycle }}&=0\\ \frac{Q_1}{T_1}+\frac{Q_2}{T_2}-\frac{Q_3}{T_3}&=0\\ \frac{2}{1000}+\frac{Q_2}{800}-\frac{1}{400}&=0\\ Q_2&=0.4 kJ\\ \text{From heat balance, }\\ Q_1+Q_2&=W+Q_3\\ 2+0.4&=W+1\\ W&=1.4 kJ \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2014:q49.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 49
pp:me:2014:q49.question:
An ideal reheat Rankine cycle operates between the pressure limits of 10 kPa and 8 MPa, with reheat being done at 4 MPa. The temperature of steam at the inlets of both turbines is 500$^{\circ}$C and the enthalpy of steam is 3185 kJ/kg at the exit of the high pressure turbine and 2247 kJ/kg at the exit of low pressure turbine. The enthalpy of water at the exit from the pump is 191 kJ/kg. Use the following table for relevant data.

Disregarding the pump work, the cycle efficiency (in percentage) is __________

detailed_solution.markdown: Given $$\begin{aligned} p_{2} &=10 \mathrm{kPa} ; \quad p_{1}=8 \mathrm{MPa} \\ p_{3} &=4 \mathrm{MPa} ; \quad h_{2}=3185 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ h_{4} &=2247 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} ; \quad h_{1}=3399 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ h_{3} &=3446 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} ; \quad h_{6}=191 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ w_{\mathrm{T}} &=\left(h_{1}-h_{2}\right)+\left(h_{3}-h_{4}\right) \\ q_{s} &=\left(h_{1}-h_{6}\right)+\left(h_{3}-h_{2}\right) \\ \therefore \quad w_{T} &=(3399-3185)+(3446-2247) \\ &=1413 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ q_{\mathrm{s}} &=(3399-191)+(3446-3185) \\ &=3469 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ \eta &=\frac{w_{\mathrm{T}}}{q_{\mathrm{s}}}=\frac{1413}{3469}=0.4073 \\ &=40.73 \% \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2014:q50.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 50
pp:me:2014:q50.question: Jobs arrive at a facility at an average rate of 5 in an 8 hour shift. The arrival of the jobs follows Poisson distribution. The average service time of a job on the facility is 40 minutes. The service time follows exponential distribution. Idle time (in hours) at the facility per shift will be

detailed_solution.markdown:
$\lambda=\frac{5}{8}$

$\mu=\frac{60}{40} \cdot \frac{3}{2}$

Probability of idleness $=1-\frac{\lambda}{\mu}$

$=1-\frac{5}{8} \times \frac{2}{3}=\frac{7}{12}$

Idle time (in hrs) per shift $=\frac{7}{12} \times 8$

$=\frac{14}{3}$

pp:me:2014:q51.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 51
pp:me:2014:q51.question: A metal rod of initial length $L_{0}$  is subjected to a drawing process. The length of the rod at any instant is given by the expression, $L(t)=L_{0}(1+t^2)$  , where t is the time in minutes. The true strain rate (in $min^{-1}$) at the end of one minute is  _______

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} L(t)&= L_{0}\left(1+t^{2}\right) \\ \Rightarrow d L&= L_{0} \times 2 t d t \\ \text{As }\quad d\epsilon _{T}&=\frac{d L}{L} \\ d \varepsilon_{T}&=\frac{L_{0} 2 t d t}{L_{0}\left(1+t^{2}\right)} \\ \frac{d \epsilon_{T}}{d t} &=\frac{2 t}{1+t^{2}} \\ \text{at}\qquad t &=1 \mathrm{min} \\ \frac{d \epsilon_{T}}{d t}&=\frac{2 \times 1}{1+t^{2}}=1 \; {min} ^{-1} \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2014:q52.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 52
pp:me:2014:q52.question: During pure orthogonal turning operation of a hollow cylindrical pipe, it is found that the thickness of the chip produced is 0.5 mm. The feed given to the zero degree rake angle tool is 0.2 mm/rev. The shear strain produced during the operation is _______

detailed_solution.concept: Manufacturing Engineering - Machining and Machine Tool Operation
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} \gamma &=\cot \phi+\tan (\phi-\alpha) \\ \text { Given, } \alpha&=0 \\ &=0.2 \mathrm{mm} \\ t_{c} &=0.5 \mathrm{mm} \\ r &=\frac{t}{t_{c}}=\frac{0.2}{0.5}=0.4 \\ \tan \phi &=\frac{r \cos \alpha}{1-r \sin \alpha}=r \\ \therefore \gamma(\text { shear strain }) &=\cot \phi+\tan (\phi-\alpha) \\ &=\frac{1+\tan ^{2} \phi}{\tan \phi}=\frac{1+0.4^{2}}{0.4} \\ &=\frac{1.16}{0.4}=2.9 \end{aligned}$$
